original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: In the abelian rank-one model with any number of dirty auxiliary scalar registers, classify eight-call words whose rational paid-frame span has dimension 4 for three invertible 3x3 data targets.
scope_change_reason: The card allows a fixed larger register count inside a stated alphabet. This package keeps the abelian rank-one alphabet, adds any number of dirty restored auxiliaries, and narrows the question to frame span exactly 4. It does not repeat the three-register census and it does not introduce a nonabelian alphabet. The narrowing matters because the dirty-auxiliary lemmas already exclude spans at most 3 and at least 7 at eight calls, and the published span-four 2x2 step is stated only for exactly three scalar registers.
bottleneck_link: A span-four word with eight calls and a dirty auxiliary would be a completed saving against the nine-call column construction in this bit model. The classification leaves only a five-call 2x2 word of span 3. No such word is constructed here, and the selected frontier is unchanged.
stop_rule: Stop after the span-four classification and its finite identity checks. Do not enumerate 120^5 words, do not rerun the three-register census, and do not treat spans 5 or 6 in this package.
evidence: PROOF.md classifies span 4. Full support and the 1+1+1 block partition need at least nine calls. The only remaining eight-call shape is the 1+2 partition with exactly three calls on the 1x1 block and five calls on the 2x2 block, projected span exactly 3. Shorter span-four words are excluded. verify.py prints PASS_SPAN4_AUXILIARY_STRUCTURE after the polynomial, support-pattern, call-budget and nine-call controls. Lemmas 1 and 2 are cited, not re-proved. Spans 5 and 6 stay open. No kappa change.
author: unpaidmoon
ai_assistance: Substantial drafting of the argument and of the finite checker by Cursor Grok. The cited predecessor lemmas were not re-derived by the assistant.

open_questions.question: Does a five-call word exist for three invertible 2x2 targets, rational frame span exactly 3, and at least one dirty auxiliary register?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the only remaining route to an eight-call span-four word for three invertible 3x3 targets with dirty auxiliaries.
open_questions.first_step: Write an arbitrary-register disjoint-subset argument at relation rank exactly 2, or run a normal-form scalar search in that relation rank.
open_questions.blocked_by: At four registers there are 120 idempotents, so 120^5 ordered words are infeasible here. A degree-1 tensor balance does not forbid five calls: a cancelling pair multiplies to the identity and preserves that balance.

open_questions.question: Can three invertible 3x3 targets be reached in eight calls with dirty auxiliaries when the rational frame span has dimension 5 or 6?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Those are the other two dimensions left open by the dirty-auxiliary lemmas at eight calls.
open_questions.first_step: Extend the two-relation disjoint-subset analysis from three registers to an arbitrary register count, then return to span five.
open_questions.blocked_by: The pattern-plane classification and common-J calculation in the three-register proof have not been redone for 120 projectors. This package does not attempt that search.
